scope: Only named completed reference/prefix profiles; no running d18 stream was read. No source edits or new simulation.
conclusion: Evidence does not support stale mu=0.5 in the d12 mu=0.75 original. Both original and replay show multi-frame friction/load ratios near 0.75; d06 mu=0.5 independently shows ratios near 0.5.

filters.single_wall_geometry: abs(normal_z)<0.03*N; one straight-wall side load>0.95*N; opposite side<0.01*N; excluded wall load<0.01*N; abs(friction_z)>0.95*friction_vector_norm
filters.post_speed: single_wall_geometry and abs(post-step COM vz)>0.2 mm/s
filters.pre_dissipative: single_wall_geometry and abs(previous-step COM vz)>0.2 mm/s and previous COM vz * current friction_z < 0
filters.interpretation: Axis-dominated force/slip screens, not proof of strictly quasistatic sliding; impulse response can reverse the post-step velocity.
filters.pose_difference_slip: single_wall_geometry plus magnitude of friction-load-weighted axial tangential velocity >0.2mm/s and >90% of tangent velocity norm, and total current friction-force dot finite-pose-difference anchor velocity <0. Velocity follows the same rigid-peg local point from previous to current pose; friction points themselves are not paired between frames.

reported_first_replay_threshold_failure.interpretation: Both streams have zero loaded normal and friction forces at sample1594. All-contact counts include unloaded detection points. Small state differences already exist at1593;1594 is the stored first tolerance failure, not the first bit-level divergence.

repeated_pretilt_trajectory_patterns.interpretation: Repeated aligned-contact trajectory pattern only; no engine/cache cause is established.
Repeated aligned-contact trajectory pattern only; no engine/cache cause is established.

limitations: Normal points and friction anchors are separate API streams and are not paired by index.
A friction/load ratio is meaningful only with adequate normal load and suitable motion; static friction, multiple walls, cancelling directions and impacts can change vector ratios.
Per-step API time alignment is not independently guaranteed; no global shift is applied. Current and previous COM velocities are reported because contact impulses can reverse velocity within a step.
Near-0.75 multi-frame ratios strongly contradict the specific stale-0.5 hypothesis, but do not identify why replay trajectories diverged.
The empirical ratio audit supplements material coefficient/mode readback; it is not a separately calibrated physical friction measurement.

The stricter check against previous-step COM velocity retains almost no strong-force samples. A separate rigid-pose finite-difference check is supplied; its finite-interval velocity is not proof of instantaneous quasistatic slip or solver force/velocity synchronization.
